parsed.summary: For a smooth, periodic family f and a fixed parameter p, the Lean theorem bounds every iterated coordinate derivative (any word w of length m) of slice (inverse d f) p, at any point Y, by mixedLossConstant m · C. Here C bounds |f|, the pure x-derivative of order m+5, and the pure y-derivative of order m+5 on [0,1]². This is a C^m tame estimate for the torus inverse, matching the shape of (8.19). The main caveat is the derivative count: Lean loses 5 derivatives and uses only pure derivatives, while the paper states a loss of 4 measured in the full C^{m+4} norm. The existence, uniqueness and Fourier-series parts of Lemma 8.6 are not stated here.

glossary.plain: ∂_x f(z) = Df(z)(1,0), the Fréchet derivative applied to the first coordinate direction.
glossary.note: Its junk value is 0 where f is not differentiable, but f is smooth here.

glossary.plain: For a word w ∈ {x,y}^m, the mixed derivative ∂_{w_1}⋯∂_{w_m} f.
glossary.standard_concept: mixed partial derivative of order m
glossary.note: Ranging over all w yields every derivative entering the C^m norm.

If Σ weight(k)^{-4} were not summable, the tsum would be 0 and the bound would degenerate to 0. Presumably weight(k) ~ 1+|k|, which makes the sum summable in 2D. The constant does not depend on d, and how the divisor bound (6.7) for v_t enters is not visible.

lean_claims.plain: Assume f : P × Plane → ℂ is C^∞ and periodic, p ∈ P, w is a derivative word of length m, Y ∈ Plane, and C ∈ ℝ satisfies three bounds on [0,1]²: |f(p,·)| ≤ C, |∂_x^{m+5} f(p,·)| ≤ C, and |∂_y^{m+5} f(p,·)| ≤ C (the last via swap). Then |∂_w (inverse d f)(p,Y)| ≤ C_m · C.

paper_claims.plain: For smooth zero-mean F on T², Nφ = F has a unique smooth zero-mean solution N⁻¹F given by the Fourier series Σ_{k≠0} F̂(k)/(2πi v_t·k) e^{2πik·y}. It satisfies ‖N⁻¹F‖_{C^m} ≤ C_m‖F‖_{C^{m+4}} for every m ≥ 0.

coverage.why: Lean requires order m+5 pure x- and y-derivatives plus sup|f|; the paper requires the full C^{m+4} norm. Lean loses one more derivative but needs no mixed derivatives.
Not stated in this declaration; it may live in the definition of `inverse` or in other lemmas.

flags.explanation: The paper's derivative loss is 4: ‖N⁻¹F‖_{C^m} ≤ C_m‖F‖_{C^{m+4}}. Lean assumes bounds on derivatives of order m+5, a loss of 5. A C^{m+4} bound does not imply bounds on (m+5)-th derivatives, so Lean is weaker in loss count, which matters for tame/Nash–Moser bookkeeping. Using only pure derivatives and sup|f| is a different, in some ways weaker, input norm. Neither statement directly implies the other.
